en: The Scripture on the Six-Syllable Divine Mantra King, translated by an unknown person, now appended to the Liang Records.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Jeta Grove in the kingdom of Śrāvastī. At that time...
There was a female outcaste from a non-Buddhist sect who exclusively practiced various evils, such as incantations, talismans, and sorcery;
she also served mountain deities, tree deities, and the spirits dwelling beneath trees.
The sun, moon, five planets, Southern Dipper, and Northern Pole Star—
all manner of *wangliang*, miscellaneous demons, and malevolent spirits—
confound the Venerable Ānanda and all virtuous people.
There were as many such [beings] as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
At that moment, the Tathāgata, seeing that Ānanda was dazed and bewildered,
felt compassion for all beings.
I shall now expound this King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtra,
which was spoken by previous Buddhas and which I now likewise speak.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:

Antare | Pandare | Karaje | Kiyuje | Tiṣyapate | Bindupate | Dhatule | Dhakudatile | Dhakumate | Sumate | Antara | Pandara | Tandara | Tidhura | Anandha | Mandhapate | Ana | Anaya | Mathu | Mapate | Karatha | Kiyula | Bodhagamī | Tiṣyapate | Bindumate | Arava | Gambhate | Vitha | Vidhini | Jitha | Vidhini | Svāhā! If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether they have already done it, or are about to do it—
whether they be gods, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Whether they be hungry ghosts (preta),
kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, piśācas, apasmāras, or upasmaras.
Whether they be Jīvakas, Kharoṣṭhas, Vedas, or Upavedas;
whether they be śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas.
Whether they be Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, or Śūdras;
whether they be Mātaṅga women, Caṇḍālas, or Caṇḍāla women;
or whether they be slaves or servants.
Whether they be men or women,
whether they be followers of external paths or Nirgranthas,
or whether they be male or female renunciants of external paths.
All such various forms of curses and *gū*-sorcery can be neutralized by this King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtra.
If they are enacted in the heavens, I shall extinguish them in the heavens.
If it acts within the world, it perishes within the world;
if it acts within the Milky Way, it perishes within the Milky Way;
if it acts within empty space, it perishes within empty space.
If one acts upon the earth, one extinguishes it upon the earth;
if one acts beneath the earth, one extinguishes it beneath the earth;
if one acts beyond the eight boundaries, one extinguishes it beyond the eight boundaries.
If one practices within the six directions, it is extinguished within the six directions.
If one practices amidst the drifting winds, it is extinguished amidst the drifting winds.
If one practices at the edge of the great waters of the four seas, it is extinguished at the edge of the great waters of the four seas.
If one acts on the banks of a river, it is extinguished on the banks of that river.
If one acts on the banks of the Huai or Ji rivers, it is extinguished on the banks of those rivers.
If one acts on the banks of a pond or a marsh, it is extinguished on the banks of that pond or marsh.
If it was committed near a body of water, it is extinguished near a body of water;
if it was committed near a great mountain, it is extinguished near a great mountain;
if it was committed near the Five Peaks, it is extinguished near the Five Peaks.
If one acts among the Five Peaks, one perishes among the Five Peaks;
if one acts at the edge of a pit or valley, one perishes at the edge of a pit or valley;
if one acts within a pit or valley, one perishes within a pit or valley.
If he acts at the edge of a dense forest, let him cease there at the edge of the dense forest;
if he acts within a dense forest, let him cease there within the dense forest;
if he acts at the edge of a tree, let him cease there at the edge of the tree.
If one acts beneath a tree, one ceases beneath a tree;
if one acts by the side of a great highway, one ceases by the side of a great highway;
if one acts upon a great highway, one ceases upon a great highway.
If it was made at the edge of a small crossroads, extinguish it at the edge of a small crossroads;
if it was made outside a city gate, extinguish it outside a city gate;
if it was made inside a city, extinguish it inside a city.
If it is made outside the palace gates, extinguish it at the outer palace gates;
if it is made inside the palace, extinguish it within the palace;
if it is made by a Brahmin, extinguish them all completely.
If it was committed near a cemetery, one should extinguish it there at the cemetery;
if it was committed within a cemetery, one should extinguish it there within the cemetery;
if it was committed near a wall, one should extinguish it there at the wall.
If it arises within a house, one should extinguish it within the house;
if it arises in a shed, one should extinguish it in the shed;
if it arises at the side of a pillar, one should extinguish it at the side of the pillar.
If it was made beneath the base of a pillar, one should extinguish it beneath the base of a pillar.
If it was made on the edge of the dust-sprinkling, one should extinguish it on the edge of the dust-sprinkling.
If it was made in the midst of the dust-sprinkling, one should extinguish it in the midst of the dust-sprinkling.
If one commits [an offense] near a well, one must extinguish it near a well;
if one commits it within a well, one must extinguish it within a well;
if one commits it near a mortar and millstone, one must extinguish it near a mortar and millstone.
If one commits it near a hearth or stove, one shall extinguish it near a hearth or stove;
if one commits it within a hearth or stove, one shall extinguish it within a hearth or stove;
if one commits it near a fire, one shall extinguish it near a fire.
If one commits it amidst fire, one should extinguish it amidst fire.
If one commits it near a latrine, one should extinguish it near a latrine.
If one commits it within a latrine, one should extinguish it within a latrine.
If it arises at the edge of a vehicle or its equipment, it ceases at the edge of the vehicle or its equipment.
If it arises within the vehicle or its equipment, it ceases within the vehicle or its equipment.
If it arises at the edge of a saddle, horse, or harness, it ceases at the edge of the saddle, horse, or harness.
If it occurs at the edge of a bed or mat, one should extinguish it at the edge of the bed or mat.
If it occurs in the middle of a bed or mat, one should extinguish it within the bed or mat.
If it occurs at the edge of a robe, blanket, woolen rug, or mattress, one should extinguish it at the edge of the robe, blanket, woolen rug, or mattress.
If it arises within boots or a hat, it ceases within the boots or the hat.
If it arises within miscellaneous utensils, it ceases within the miscellaneous utensils.
If it arises within food or drink, it ceases within the food or drink.
If those who are close associates perform them, they shall all be extinguished.
If performed at night, they are extinguished at night;
if performed during the day, they are extinguished during the day.
Whatever [obstacles] are constantly created day and night, this mantra shall extinguish them all.
This mantra can sever the paths of the mantras of Śakra;
it can sever the paths of the mantras of Brahmā.
It can sever the paths of incantations of the Four Heavenly Kings,
as well as all paths of spells, demonic ghosts, and esoteric arts;
if anyone should cast evil curses or incantations against a certain person, it can sever them all.
And all poisons shall be utterly extinguished.
Whether it be caused by a khaṇḍa, a vetāla,
a jīva, or a pūtana, all such things shall be utterly extinguished.
All evils are completely exhausted, and all virtues fill their place.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.
By means of these words of truth, may there be well-being.
May [Name] be peaceful by day and peaceful by night, always peaceful day and night.
May they live for a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because in the world, there is nothing superior to the Buddha.
That which is offered to the Celestial Honored One is reverently upheld by the assembly of deities.
Should there be those who practice evil incantations or paths—
whether they have already done so, are doing so, or are about to do so— [this shall be applied].
Whether it be those who act with malice, those who have attained accomplishment, or those who have not yet attained accomplishment—
all such things shall be extinguished. Furthermore, all poisons capable of harming people shall be entirely eliminated by this King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtra.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*kha-ji kha-zhu kha-vi-ji gan-shu gan-shu ta-ji ba-ji*. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether they have already done it, or are about to do it—
whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Furthermore, all malevolent spells and curses shall be entirely extinguished.
Whether they are caused by khaṣāntas, vidyādharas, or pūtanas, all such acts shall be entirely extinguished.
All evils are utterly exhausted, and all virtues fill their place.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.
By means of these words of truth, may there be well-being.
May such-and-such a person be at peace by day and at peace by night, always at peace day and night.
May they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because in the world, nothing is more wondrous than the Dharma.
Revered by gods and humans, honored and received by all māras, free from desire and unattached, he then spoke this mantra:
*kha-ji kha-zhu kha-vi-ji gan-shu gan-shu ta-ji pa-ji*. For what reason?
In this world, nothing is more noble than the Saṅgha.
It is a field of merit for the virtuous, revered by sages and saints, and protected by all that is good.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Kha-ti kha-zhu kha-vi-ti gan-shu gan-shu ta-ti ba-ti tou-te a-mi-te a-çu-te. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person.
Whether it be the compounding of poisons,
whether genuine or counterfeit, or any unlawful act performed,
whether in a previous life or in this present life.
All the various evils of one's conduct and all grave transgressions shall be entirely extinguished.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

Makhyopa | Umota | Sīdane | Khayuta | Pate | Sīdane | Bindumatī | Citi | Citadeva | Sīdane | Abhre | Candrabhre | Svāhā. If there is anyone who recites and upholds this King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtra.
If one could cause a withered tree to sprout branches and leaves again through incantation,
how much more so for a human being?
May such-and-such a person attain a hundred years of life and witness a hundred autumns.
That which was spoken by all Buddhas and transmitted by Ānanda—
if anyone reads and recites it until they have mastered it, they will all protect themselves;
all evils will stay far from their person, and they will dwell constantly with what is wholesome.
If one recites this for another, it can eliminate that person's manifold sufferings, evils, and afflictions.
The reciter must abstain from the five pungent roots and maintain a sincere, pure mind before they may perform this rite.
Thus, all calamities and misfortunes will be left behind without exception, and there will be nothing auspicious that is not beneficial.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

He-he-cari | He-he-nami | He-he-pukudha-mati | He-he-pukudha | Ni-kuśa | He-he-niha | Dha-kha-umda | Ni-viśa | Kha-umda | Iṇe | Miṇe | Dhāpe | Dhādhape | Svāhā | Namo buddhāya Avalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya.
Homage to the Dharma.
Homage to the Saṃgha of Bhikṣus.
I pay homage to that Great Being.
Thereupon he spoke this divine mantra:
"May this mantra be ever auspicious!
Avalokiteśvara, contemplate my body; Avalokiteśvara, contemplate my body, out of compassion for me."
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

U-ha-ni | Mu-ha-ni | A-da-ni | A-da | Vi-a-da | Ja-vi-ni | Dam-vi-ni | An-ta-le | Na-da-le | Si-pi-ti | An-ta | Ra-ba-si | Sa-lu-dou | Shuai-ta-ba-lo | Dou-shuai-ta | Mao-dan-ja-po | Ye-dan-po | Ye-mu-he-ye | Ni-po-lo | Ye-ye-po-mo | Luo-ti | Pan-mo-che-ti | Lu-lou-zhi-ta | Ban-ta-si | Zhi-ta-ban-ta-si | Svi-pa-ha. This mantra is able to protect against all calamities and hardships.
This pure and radiant liberation, free from defilement, contemplates all and delivers beings from every hardship, delusion, and malevolent māras. In this present life,
it protects the body from lions,
mad elephants, tigers, wolves, and monkeys.
May all venomous beasts that seek to harm people be completely bound.
For the sake of [Name] and his traveling companions,
may there be nothing inauspicious wherever the power of this mantra is directed.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*Cili cili, ciri, modgali, candali, rakṣa rakṣa, rāya, svāhā! Namo buddhāya!*
Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṃgha.
May this mantra bring great auspiciousness.
When skillfully employing this dhāraṇī method,
on the day it is to be used, one should bathe until fresh and clean, thoroughly removing all impurities and filth.
One must not engage in sexual intercourse, nor consume the five pungent vegetables, nor drink alcohol.
While eating meat, hold its cord with a white cotton thread;
recite the mantra seven times, tying a knot once for each repetition.
If you are involved in legal matters or slandered by others, [perform this rite].
Should there be strife or contention,
or curses and incantations,
as well as all manner of evils, they shall all be extinguished.
Having finished the incantation, tie this thread to the person's clean garment or sash.
After the ritual is concluded,
invite the Buddha and the Sangha to burn various kinds of famous incense.

He immediately sat in meditation, read Mahāyāna sūtras, and established offering assemblies for the midday meal according to his capacity, both great and small, to repay the Buddha’s compassionate grace. He vowed to liberate himself and others, praying forever to sever the eight difficulties; as his virtuous aspirations were fulfilled, he spoke this mantra:

Dharmade, Yaśapati, Vasa, Upade, Upapati, Uttaraṇi, Akṣaya-pati, Anuśanti-mudra, Paravakṣiti, Parava-kṣitu, Svāhā. Homage to the immeasurable Buddhas of the three periods—future, past, and present—who eternally abide.
The Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and Maitreya Śūraṅgama-samādhi;
the request to the Buddha for Avalokiteśvara to eliminate and subdue poisonous harms;
and the six-syllable phrases of the Ākāśagarbha, Ratnaketu, and Mayūrī Dhāraṇīs.
The Bodhisattva Resolute Mind and the Bodhisattva Untainted each proclaimed that all those who have attained the Way are noble sages;
they take refuge in such a multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
As before, one should recite the names of the Triple Gem three times.
Thereafter, one should recite this Great Divine Dhāraṇī mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Karaṇīmatīvinudaniyaḥ (or Karaṇīmatīvinudani)
Gadīvaraviśākhaśūraḥ
Varidānudisaṃdhāpati (or Varidānudisaṃdhapati)
Uttara-niṣadha-kaśa-dha-saravi-śa.
Śāṇḍakāriśavasana
Bhagavati kauśalya-vāsini.
Aṇu-saṃte vi-saṃte jite.
Ajite tvaṃ nāgade ajatvaṃ nāgade.
Avāsariśavaraṇī-mūre mūre.
Vatene śanīvara luk.
Sūlipati-juti-bharaluḥ
Suvimale amale.
This mantra can eliminate all darkness; it is upheld by the Tathāgata, revered by the devas, protected by benevolent deities, and understood by Brahmā.
Śakra serves it, and the World-Protectors guard and protect it;
the great sages and noble ones have definitively resolved upon it, uphold it, and harmonize with it;
through it, sentient beings are liberated from their bonds.
From the Four Heavenly Kings downward, including the multitudes of common people, they sever their afflictions and subdue demonic adversaries.
They transform non-Buddhists, causing them to destroy evil and turn toward the good,
thereby eliminating their hearts of contention, envy, sophistry, and arrogance.
He increases his roots of goodness through every act of benevolence;
as a Dharma Master, he transcends worldly concerns and does not abandon the great assembly.
He delights others in their studies and guards the sacred scriptures.
This profound treasury of Dharma benefits the Three Jewels and takes pity upon all classes of sentient beings;
such are the benefits that adorn its manifold meanings.
This dharani phrase is named the "Inexhaustible Treasury. It is a protection that can protect even where no other protection exists.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who can read and recite it, they shall obtain thirty-three kinds of freedom from doubt, fear, and difficulty.
Using this dhāraṇī method, rise early at dawn, wash your hands and rinse your mouth, burn incense, and perform three prostrations; then recite it.
In whatever place you go, maintain speech and conversation [in accordance with the precepts].
In all directions, he is impermanent and unsurpassed;
the multitude honors and respects him, those who see him rejoice,
and his enemies are subdued— such are the benefits.
This is for those who single-mindedly uphold these dharani verses.
From the *Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the King of Six-Syllable Divine Mantras*.
